title: Distance 1
content:
Once the dust settled from their staged duel, Wen Ning’s terrifyingly rabid display earned him a grim new moniker, though that is a tale for another time. Despite taking a blade clean through his abdomen, Wei Wuxian could not have cared less. He nonchalantly shoved his spilling intestines back into his belly, commanded Wen Ning to hunt down a few wandering wraiths, and hauled several massive sacks of potatoes back up the mountain.

Upon his return to the Burial Mounds, Wen Qing patched him up while ripping him a new one—she had strictly told him to buy radish seeds, not potatoes.

Life settled into a mundane, tranquil rhythm after that. Wei Wuxian led the fifty-odd Wen remnants through a daily routine of tilling fields, building shacks, refining corpses, and crafting spiritual tools. Whenever boredom struck, he amused himself by roughhousing with Wen Yuan, Wen Qing’s cousin’s little boy, who was barely a toddler. He would hang the kid from tree branches or bury him up to his neck in the dirt, shamelessly sweet-talking him with lies about how soaking up sunlight and a little water would make him sprout faster. Naturally, every stunt earned him an earful of Wen Qing’s fiery wrath.

A few months drifted by without incident. Beyond the outside world painting Wei Wuxian as an increasingly monstrous villain, nothing escalated.

Opportunities to slip down the mountain were few and far between. The suffocating, malevolent yin energy of the Burial Mounds was tethered solely to his personal suppression; he could neither venture too far nor linger away for long. Still, being restless by nature and allergic to staying put, he frequently sneaked into the nearest settlement under the flimsy pretense of buying groceries, taking his sweet time wandering the bustling streets. Recognizing that Wen Yuan had spent far too long cooped up playing in corpse dirt, Wei Wuxian decided it was high time the two-year-old saw the outside world, scoping him up on his next errand run.

Having made the trek countless times, Wei Wuxian navigated the market stalls with practiced ease. Rolling up to a vegetable vendor, he pawed through the wooden crates before dramatically hoisting a spud into the air, yelling in outrage, "These potatoes are sprouting green!"

The vendor stiffened, instantly on guard. "What's it to you?!"

Wei Wuxian countered shamelessly, "Give me a discount."

Wen Yuan had been clinging to his pant leg like a burr the entire time. As Wei Wuxian paced back and forth, haggling over half a copper coin, the toddler’s stubby little arms eventually gave out. He let go to shake out his cramped fingers, but in that fleeting second, a surging wave of market pedestrians jostled him, sweeping him into the crowd and stripping him of all sense of direction. From his knee-high vantage point, Wei Wuxian’s long stride and black leather boots were nowhere to be found; his vision was walled in by a chaotic sea of mud-caked, graying hemp trousers. Utterly bewildered, he wobbled forward in a daze until he bumped headfirst into someone's leg.

The stranger wore spotless, snow-white boots. Moving at a calm, unhurried pace, he stopped dead in his tracks the second the child collided with him.

Trembling, Wen Yuan tilted his chin up. His eyes traced from the carved jade pendant hanging at the stranger’s hip, up to a sash embroidered with delicate cloud motifs, past an immaculate, rigidly folded collar, and finally landed upon a pair of pale glass-like eyes that radiated pure winter frost.

The towering stranger gazed down at him with an unyielding, severe chill, and terror instantly seized the toddler's heart.

Meanwhile, Wei Wuxian had spent half an eternity picking over the produce, ultimately turning his nose up at the sprouting spuds. Eating poison wasn't on his agenda today, especially since the vendor refused to slash the price. The hawker sneered, turning his back. It was only when Wei Wuxian wheeled around that his stomach plummeted—Wen Yuan had vanished into thin air. In an absolute panic, he bolted down the street scanning the crowd, when the piercing wails of a distressed child cut through the air. He dashed toward the sound. Not far off, a crowd of nosy bystanders had formed a tight, gossiping circle, craning their necks and pointing. Shoving his way through the pack, Wei Wuxian’s eyes lit up.

There, looking impossibly stiff in his sweeping white robes with Bichen slung across his back, stood Lan Wangji. Trapped in the center of the bustling mob, he wore a rare, priceless look of sheer, panicked helplessness. Looking down, Wei Wuxian nearly folded in half laughing. Splayed on the cobblestones right before Lan Wangji’s pristine boots was Wen Yuan, bawling his little eyes out with tears and snot streaming down his flushed cheeks. Lan Wangji stood frozen—leaving felt cruel, staying felt awkward, reaching out felt improper, and speaking felt impossible. He merely stared down with grave solemnity, his mind visibly short-circuiting over how to handle the miniature crisis.

A busybody cracking melon seeds between her teeth muttered, "What’s going on here? That tiny thing is screeching loud enough to wake the dead."

A bystander piped up with absolute conviction, "Must've gotten a tongue-lashing from his old man."

Hearing the words "his old man," Wei Wuxian snorted, covering his mouth in the crowd. Lan Wangji snapped his chin up instantly, denying it flatly: "I am not."

Wen Yuan, completely oblivious to the crowd's idle chatter, reacted on pure toddler instinct. When children are terrified, they cry out for whoever feels safest, which meant he choked out through broken hiccups, "Daddy! Daddy, waaah...!"

The crowd seized on it instantly. "Hear that?! Told you, that's his father!"

An old woman with an eagle eye chimed in, "Dead ringer for his dad! That nose was carved from the exact same mold, no doubt about it!"

A sympathetic soul sighed, "Poor little creature, crying like his heart is breaking. Did his father scold him that badly?"

A frustrated cart-driver shouted from the edge, "What's the holdup up there?! Clear the lane, will you? My wheelbarrow can't get through!"

A matron scolded loudly, "Pick the boy up and soothe him, for heaven's sake! Letting your own flesh and blood wail in the dirt—what kind of father does that?!"

An older man waved a hand, offering a worldly take: "He’s so young, must be his first time as a dad. I was the exact same way back in the day, totally clueless. Once your wife pops out a few more, you get the hang of it. Parenthood takes time..."

Someone tried coaxing the toddler, "Hush now, sweetheart, don't cry. Where’s your mommy?"

"Yeah, where’s the mother? Dad is utterly useless, so where’s the mom?"

Beneath the overwhelming barrage of unsolicited neighborhood parenting advice, Lan Wangji’s expression twisted into something extraordinarily bizarre.

Pity the Second Young Master of Lan, who had spent his entire life hailed as heaven's chosen prodigy, a walking textbook of elegance and moral virtue, only to find himself publicly pilloried by an entire street of elderly gossips. Wei Wuxian was practically dying of laughter, but seeing that Wen Yuan was on the verge of crying himself hoarse, he finally stepped out of the shadows. Feigning absolute shock, he called out, "Huh? Lan Zhan?"

Lan Wangji’s head whipped around, their eyes colliding. For reasons he couldn't quite unpack, Wei Wuxian averted his gaze for a split second. Recognizing the voice, Wen Yuan scrambled up from the dirt, streaking tears down his cheeks as he sprinted forward and latched right back onto Wei Wuxian’s calf. The crowd buzzed again, confused. "Wait, who’s this one now? Where’s the mother? Which one of them is the actual dad?!"

Wei Wuxian waved his hands at the mob. "Show's over, folks! Break it up, break it up!"

Seeing that the drama had fizzled out, the onlookers reluctantly dispersed. Wei Wuxian turned back, flashing a cheeky grin. "What a coincidence! Lan Zhan, what brings you all the way out to Yiling?"

Lan Wangji answered flatly, "A night-hunt. Passing through."

Hearing his tone remain as calm and even as ever—carrying not a shred of contempt or hostility—a subtle knot unraveled in Wei Wuxian’s chest.

Lan Wangji’s eyes dipped downward, his voice slow: "...This child?"

Relief made Wei Wuxian’s tongue reckless, blurting out without thinking, "Gave birth to him myself."

Lan Wangji’s brow twitched. Wei Wuxian let out a hearty laugh. "Just kidding, obviously! He belongs to someone else; I just brought him out to stretch his legs. What did you do to him just now, anyway? How’d you send him into hysterics?"

Lan Wangji’s tone was clipped: "I did nothing."

Wen Yuan was still sniffling, face buried in Wei Wuxian’s pant leg. Understanding dawned on Wei Wuxian instantly. While Lan Wangji was undeniably stunning, a toddler that young possessed zero appreciation for ethereal bone structure; all the boy saw was an intimidating, freezing block of ice who looked perpetually aggrieved, and the sheer sternness had terrified him to tears. Wei Wuxian hoisted Wen Yuan into his arms, tossing him gently up and down to coax him with sweet words. Catching sight of a peddler grinning from ear to ear while watching the circus, Wei Wuxian pointed toward the colorful wares dangling from the shoulder-pole. "Look there, A-Yuan. Isn't that pretty?"

Distracted, Wen Yuan sniffled, rubbing his nose. "...Pretty."

Wei Wuxian nudged him. "Smell nice, too?"

"Smells nice."

The street hawker jumped at the opening: "Pretty as a picture and fragrant to boot! Treat the young master to one, sir!"

Wei Wuxian leaned down, grinning. "Do you want it?"

Assuming he was getting a present, Wen Yuan nodded shyly. "Want."

Wei Wuxian immediately pivoted on his heel, taking off in the opposite direction. "Haha, alright! Let's go!"

Wen Yuan was struck dumb, fat tears welling up in his eyes all over again. Lan Wangji, who had watched the petty cruelty unfold from the sidelines, couldn't stomach it any longer. "Why didn't you buy it for him?"

Wei Wuxian turned around, utterly baffled. "Why on earth should I buy it for him?"

Lan Wangji frowned. "You asked if he wanted it. Does that not imply you intended to buy it?"

Wei Wuxian shot back playfully, "Asking is asking, buying is buying! Since when does asking someone if they want something mean you're obligated to purchase it?"

The brazen, backward logic left Lan Wangji thoroughly speechless. He glared at Wei Wuxian for a long moment before dropping his gaze to the trembling toddler, whose lip had started quivering under the intense stare.

After a beat, Lan Wangji spoke to Wen Yuan, his voice dipping low: "Which one... do you want?"

Before the kid could process the question, Lan Wangji pointed toward the peddler's baskets. "Everything in there—pick which one you want."

Wen Yuan stared up at him in wide-eyed shock, petrified to even draw breath.

Half an incense stick later, Wen Yuan had finally dried his tears. His little hands couldn't stop patting his robes, his pockets bulging with the staggering mountain of knick-knacks Lan Wangji had showered upon him. Seeing the tears dry up, Lan Wangji seemed to breathe an inward sigh of relief.

Then, cheeks flushing a rosy pink, Wen Yuan quietly shuffled over and wrapped his stubby arms around Lan Wangji’s calf.

Looking down to find a tiny human clamped to his shin, Lan Wangji froze completely.

Wei Wuxian howled with laughter. "Hahaha! Lan Zhan, congratulations! He’s claimed you! Whoever he likes, he clamps onto their leg and refuses to let go!"

Lan Wangji took two deliberate steps. Sure enough, Wen Yuan clung to his boot like an oversized cicada, showing zero intention of releasing his grip, hugging him remarkably tight.

Wei Wuxian clapped Lan Wangji’s shoulder warmly. "Look, night-hunting can wait. How about we grab a bite to eat first?"

Lan Wangji flicked his eyes up, tone flat as water: "A meal?"

"Yeah, food! Don't be so stiff," Wei Wuxian wheedled. "It’s not every day you grace Yiling with your presence, and running into you like this is fate! Let’s catch up. Come on, my treat!"

Between Wei Wuxian dragging him by the elbow and Wen Yuan acting as a five-pound ankle weight, Lan Wangji was essentially hauled into a nearby restaurant. Once settled in a private dining room, Wei Wuxian kicked back. "Order whatever you like!"

Lan Wangji was deposited onto the woven mat, his gaze sweeping over the bamboo menu strips. "You order."

"I'm treating, so the guest orders," Wei Wuxian insisted. "Get whatever sounds good, don't hold back." Having skipped the poisonous sprouted potatoes earlier, he actually had silver in his pouch to cover the tab. Lan Wangji wasn't one for performative modesty; after a brief pause, he began placing the order. Listening to him rattle off several notoriously spicy dishes with a straight face, Wei Wuxian grinned. "Not bad, Lan Zhan! I thought you Gusu folks couldn't stomach chili peppers. Turns out you like a little kick. Care for some wine?"

Lan Wangji gave a slight shake of his head. Wei Wuxian sighed, amused. "Even miles away from home, you follow the rules to the letter. Truly a model gentleman. Fine, none for you then."

Curled up at Lan Wangji’s feet, Wen Yuan lined up his treasures across the mat: little wooden sabers, tiny wooden swords, painted clay figurines, and woven straw butterflies, inventorying his loot with absolute adoration. Seeing the kid squirming against Lan Wangji’s side—making it nearly impossible for the man to lift his teacup—Wei Wuxian whistled sharply. "A-Yuan, get over here."

Wen Yuan weighed his options: on one hand was Wei Wuxian, who had buried him in the soil like a turnip two days ago; on the other was Lan Wangji, who had just bought him half a toy shop. His butt didn't budge an inch, his chubby face radiating an unambiguous message: No way.

Wei Wuxian nudged him. "Come here. You're crowding him."

Lan Wangji countered softly, "It is fine. Let him sit."

Thrilled by the pardon, Wen Yuan wrapped his arms around Lan Wangji’s thigh this time. Spinning his chopsticks into a blur, Wei Wuxian scoffed playfully, "Whoever feeds him is mother, whoever pays is father. Truly shameless."

Before long, the dishes and wine arrived, blanketing the table in a fiery sea of red chilis, alongside a small bowl of sweet almond soup Lan Wangji had specially ordered for the boy. Wei Wuxian tapped his bowl several times to get his attention, but Wen Yuan was completely absorbed, holding up two straw butterflies and muttering under his breath. First, he pitched his voice into a shy murmur for the left butterfly: "I... I love you very much,"then chimed in cheerfully for the right: "I love you very much too!" Playing out the romance between two woven insects with pure, unadulterated glee.

Wei Wuxian nearly choked on his drink, doubling over as he wheezed with laughter. "Good gods, A-Yuan, who on earth taught you that? What's with all this 'I love you, you love me'? Do you even know what liking someone means? Drop the drama and eat up—your new daddy ordered you something sweet."

Only then did Wen Yuan stash the butterflies into his pouch, scooping up his porcelain spoon to dig into the sweet soup beside Lan Wangji. Having bounced from a Qishan labor camp to the desolate Burial Mounds, his diet had been bleak at best; this sweet treat was practically high cuisine. After two bites, he couldn't stop himself, though he still had the manners to hoist the bowl toward Wei Wuxian like a prized treasure. "...Xian-gege... Gege eat."

Wei Wuxian beamed with pride. "Good boy. At least you know to pay your respects to me."

Lan Wangji murmured, "Silence during meals."

Fearing the toddler wouldn't catch the classical phrasing, he clarified in plain words: "Do not speak while eating."

Wen Yuan nodded vigorously, burying his face back in the bowl and clamping his mouth shut.

Wei Wuxian gaped. "Unbelievable. I have to yell at him five times before he listens, but one word from you and he falls right into line. Unbelievable."

Lan Wangji said evenly, "Silence during meals. You as well."

Wei Wuxian chuckled, tipping his cup back to down the liquor before idly twirling the empty porcelain between his fingers. "You really haven't changed a bit in all these years, have you? So, Lan Zhan—what are you hunting in Yiling anyway? I know the terrain like the back of my hand; want me to point you in the right direction?"

Lan Wangji replied, "No need."

Sects often engaged in classified missions that weren't meant for outsiders' ears, so Wei Wuxian didn't pry. "It's rare to run into an old acquaintance who doesn't dodge me like the plague; these past few months have bored me out of my skull. Anything major happening in the cultivation world lately?"

"What constitutes major?"

"You know, a new sect popping up, an ancestral estate being renovated, alliances forming... Just shoot the breeze, idle gossip." Since staging his defection with Jiang Cheng, he had been entirely cut off from the rumor mill, gleaning only whatever fragmented chatter he could overhear in local taverns.

Lan Wangji answered, "A wedding alliance."

Wei Wuxian paused. "Between who?"

"The Lanling Jin Sect and the Yunmeng Jiang Sect."

The porcelain cup froze in Wei Wuxian’s fingers.

He stared, stunned. "My Shi... Lady Jiang and Jin Zixuan?"

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod.

Wei Wuxian pressed, his voice tightening, "When was this arranged? When is the ceremony?!"

"In three days."

Wei Wuxian brought the cup to his lips with a trembling hand, completely oblivious to the fact that it was bone-dry. A hollow emptiness caved in his chest, an overwhelming tangle of rage, shock, bitterness, and utter helplessness.

Even though he had seen the writing on the wall before walking away from Lotus Pier, having the reality dropped on his head left a thousand words lodged like glass in his throat, desperate to scream, yet finding no outlet. Jiang Cheng hadn't even found a covert way to pass along the message. If he hadn't crossed paths with Lan Wangji today, he likely wouldn't have known until long after the vows were spoken!

Yet the rational part of his brain kicked in: even if Jiang Cheng had told him, what could he have done? Publicly, Jiang Cheng had severed all ties, and the prominent clans had bought the story hook, line, and sinker: Wei Wuxian was a disgraced rogue who held zero affiliation with the Yunmeng Jiang Sect. Even knowing the date, he couldn't step foot near the banquet to share a celebratory cup of wine. Jiang Cheng had made the right call keeping him in the dark; had he known, his reckless temper might have driven him to pull something disastrous.

After an agonizing silence, Wei Wuxian muttered under his breath, "That peacock got off easy."

He poured himself another cup. "Lan Zhan, what's your take on this marriage?"

Lan Wangji remained silent. Wei Wuxian let out a hollow chuckle. "Right, why am I asking you? What could you possibly think—you've never spared a thought for romance."

He drained the wine in a single gulp. "I know people gossip behind closed doors that my Shijie isn't good enough for Jin Zixuan. Ha. In my eyes, that bastard isn't fit to lace her boots. But against all odds..."

Against all odds, Jiang Yanli loved him.

Wei Wuxian slammed the cup onto the wood with concussive force. "Lan Zhan! You hear me? My Shijie deserves the finest man under the heavens."

He slapped the table, his features flushed with wine and unbending pride. "We were supposed to give her a grand ceremony that people would marvel at for the next hundred years—a spectacle so breathtaking that no one could ever rival it. I was supposed to watch her married in glorious splendor."

Lan Wangji murmured softly, "Mm."

Wei Wuxian scoffed bitterly. "What are you 'mm-ing' for? I won't even be there to see it."

By now, Wen Yuan had scraped the bowl clean and returned to his straw butterflies. The long, delicate antennae had knotted together into a stubborn tangle that his clumsy fingers couldn't pry apart. Seeing the toddler teetering on the verge of another meltdown, Lan Wangji gently lifted the toys from his hands, his slender fingers working the four knotted strands free in two deft movements before returning them.

Watching the exchange, Wei Wuxian shook the gloom from his mind, forcing a thin smile. "A-Yuan, don't rub your face on his robes. You've got sweet soup all over your chin; you're going to soil his clothes."

Lan Wangji produced a pristine white handkerchief, expressionlessly dabbing the sticky syrup from the boy’s mouth.

Wei Wuxian let out an appreciative whistle. "Look at you, Lan Zhan. Color me impressed—who knew you were a natural with kids? If you keep spoiling him, he's never going to come home with me..."

Suddenly, Wei Wuxian’s face drained of color. He plunged a hand into his lapel, ripping out a paper talisman that had already caught fire. The moment it cleared his robes, it dissolved into a puff of black ash. Lan Wangji’s gaze sharpened, while Wei Wuxian bolted upright. "Shit."

That talisman served as the core anchor for the warning array he had erected across the Burial Mounds. If the perimeter was breached in his absence, the barrier shattered, or a massive surge of bloodlust flared, the charm would ignite to signal an emergency. Tucking Wen Yuan firmly under his arm like a sack of grain, Wei Wuxian threw over his shoulder, "Excuse me, Lan Zhan, I have to go!"

A toy tumbled from the toddler’s pockets. "B-Butterfly!" But Wei Wuxian had already bolted down the stairs and out of the tavern. Moments later, a streak of white swept past him, Lan Wangji falling effortlessly into step at his side. Wei Wuxian panted, "Lan Zhan? Why are you following me?!"

Lan Wangji pressed the dropped straw butterfly into his palm, completely ignoring the question to demand, "Why not mount your sword?"

Wei Wuxian blurted out, "Forgot to bring it!"

Without another word, Lan Wangji’s arm hooked around his waist, hoisting him effortlessly onto Bichen as the blade surged skyward. Wen Yuan was far too young to have ever ridden a spiritual sword and should have been scared out of his wits, but Bichen’s flight was so remarkably steady that there wasn't a hint of turbulence. Seeing the townspeople below craning their necks in awe at the airborne trio, the toddler broke into giddy, delighted giggles.

Wei Wuxian let out a massive breath of relief. "Thanks!"

Lan Wangji asked, "Where to?"

Wei Wuxian pointed toward the dark peaks: "Over there!"
